fatal: No margin over the strongest baseline in any primary cell, by construction. Under good comms (the stated primary for F1-F3), KORE is central rolling-horizon ALNS with structural triggers. B3(b) is chosen on dev to be exactly that. E2's TOST therefore compares the method with itself and proves nothing. Every E1 margin is an optimizer-quality gap carried over from Phase 1, not a dynamic mechanism. RL(g.)/KORE 1.15-1.17 matches RL's static gap of about 20% (summarize_rel.py). Insertion-only/ALNS 1.07-1.13 is the textbook DVRP result that re-optimization beats insertion. Reviewers will read E1 as 'Phase-1 ALNS in an event loop', and that design already exists: Demiray et al. (arXiv 2309.09321, C&IE 2026) run event-triggered ALNS re-optimization with frozen periods, synchronization and degree of dynamism; Calvo and Capitan (T-RO 2025) and D-ITAGS (RA-L 2023) repair coalition plans online.

The one regime left for a win (C3) rests on rule 6, frozen-scope closure-local repair. That is the in-house LOC-F / CAS-INF / OPEN family, and it already tied or lost in the equal-lease pilot (pilots/trackD_integ/out/summary.txt, P7, grace 3 / max 30): LOC-F/CEN-F 0.997-1.055, CAS-INF/CEN-F 0.968-1.124, OPEN/CEN-F 1.26-1.51. The arms that won at R <= r_c re-plan out-of-contact robots from a stale-state belief, the opposite of KORE's keep-the-plan rule: CLAMP 0.824-0.978 of CEN-F, HYB 0.817-0.963, REP-G3:30 0.906-0.965. In the DAR pilot (pilots/trackD_comm2/out/dar34_summary.txt) the best arm is a one-line scope rule, INF-r. The sophisticated delivery-aware arm lost to it: DAR-r/INF-r 1.033 at R=0.15 and 1.140 at R=0.10.

Under C3, the choice of method matters less than the timeout setting and a cheap infrastructure fix, which is CBJA's collapse in a new form. Lease patience alone moves REP by 5-17% (P6: REP-G3:30/REP 0.83-0.95). It also reverses the CEN-F vs REP ranking between the default-lease pilot (P2) and the equal-patient-lease pilot (P7). A 1-per-time-unit global state beacon with 20% loss closes most of the gap (P5: REP-B1/REP 0.73-0.87 at R <= r_c). A reviewer can answer 'add a low-rate long-range beacon' and the headroom disappears.

Each KORE-specific component reduces to a rule or to cited prior art, and its ablations are predicted to be null. Not re-planning on noise is the rescheduling-nervousness result (Vieira, Herrmann and Lin, J. Sched. 2003) and ADG/TPG execution (ADG; APEX-MR, RSS 2025, which executes collaborative support actions under delays without re-planning). The consensus layer is ACBBA's timestamp rule plus its suffix-release rule. The lease reduces to a heartbeat timeout under good comms. The CRDT merge is the identity when comms are good. Coalition partners are usually within range exactly when the lease would matter: current-partner latency median is 0 even at R = 0.63 r_c (pilots/trackD/out/conn.txt). So T6, T7 and T8 are expected to come out null.
fixable: K0 fidelity and pairing: the RL rows come from DynTaskEnv, while the KORE, RH and insertion rows come from the hand-written executor (rh_pilot.Episode). The two differ in idle semantics (wait in place vs head home and re-dispatch), coalition order and back-dating. The 14-19% RL margin is not yet paired on a single simulator. Replay every method in DynTaskEnv first.

Failure detection under partitions is logically broken. A heartbeat timeout cannot tell a crashed robot from one that is out of range (an unreliable failure detector). Rule 6 cannot repair a failed robot's tasks, because the failed member is by definition outside every component. False suspicion splits coalitions and causes duplicate service. G1 assumes consistent replicas and G3 assumes eventual delivery, and D2/D3 break both. Needed: an explicit suspicion model, a rule for resolving duplicate service, and guarantees restated for C3.

Self-anchored benchmark parameters. Failure onset is drawn from U[0, 0.7 x the proposed method's ALNS makespan]; anchor it on the paper's RL(g.) makespan or an instance-intrinsic horizon. The tick mapping (100 ms = 0.1 time units) is arbitrary for a dimensionless map. Rounding each call up to one tick charges RL's roughly 6 ms forward pass at every per-agent decision, but charges KORE only per structural event, which penalizes RL by about 2-4%. Make the 1 s mapping co-primary or charge unrounded time. The 'clairvoyant' ALNS is a reference, not a bound, and it ignores delays.

Reproducibility and CRN: 25 ms wall-clock deadlines on a loaded shared host make runs non-deterministic and break paired CRN. Use fixed iteration budgets with one calibrated ms/iteration conversion, measured on a quiet pinned core.

Equal infrastructure gaps. (1) RL(s.N) re-rolled from the current state at every structural event is an online rollout policy, symmetric to KORE's re-solve, so it must be a baseline. The RL64+ALNS hybrid, which statically ties ALNS at 0.995-0.999, must be run online too. (2) Every method's lease (grace and max) must be tuned on dev with the same budget, since P6 shows 5-17% swings. (3) CEN-F must get the same rally/idle policy, and a beacon arm.

The T1 simple-rule control is a strawman. Insertion without reorganization (ES@0) is the wrong comparison, because 30 iterations (3 ms) already come within 1.9-3.4% of 3000 iterations. The collapse test must be KORE vs B6 (regret re-construction with restarts at the same 25 ms budget). SA-BT R1 already fails the 3% bar: 1.009 [0.997, 1.020].

Statistics. The 3 CRN seeds are nested in 50 instances, so bootstrap over instances (cluster) or fit a mixed model instead of treating 150 rows as independent. Failure counted as 200 dominates mean log r; report success separately and use a censored or rank statistic. Replace E2's self-TOST with a comparison against a different central policy (every-event or periodic RH). Power E4 from the pilot SDs, where the expected effects are 2-7% at R ~ r_c.

Forking paths: the scenario families were chosen after the pilots, and noise was demoted to a 'control' once it showed parity. Freeze the families, margins and the per-method tuning protocol now, and report every family, F0 included.

Novelty check still open: read DODRL-HMRTA (Neurocomputing 2026, doi 10.1016/j.neucom.2026.135060, 'HMRTA with dynamic uncertainties'; abstract closed), the CSCWD 2026 proactive fault-recovery paper (successor pre-assignment) and the RA-L 2026 LLM-MILP dynamic scheduling paper. All three cite HeteroMRTA. Do this before claiming the first dynamic HeteroMRTA benchmark.

The CBBA-family baselines (CBTA, CBGA, coupled-constraint CBBA, D-ITAGS-style, Messing-style) are reimplementations with our own bid and insertion kernels, which is the CBJA baseline trap. Disclose this and do not count wins over them as external SOTA evidence. Per-event time at 150x500 is still unmeasured (K5).
prior_work: Demiray, Tolga, Yucel, 'An Optimization Framework for a Dynamic Multi-Skill Workforce Scheduling and Routing Problem with Time Windows and Synchronization Constraints', arXiv 2309.09321 (C&IE 2026): ALNS re-optimization triggered by new tasks or elapsed time, frozen part of the plan, synchronization, degree-of-dynamism study. This is KORE rules 1, 2 and 4 in centralized OR form. https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09321

Calvo and Capitan, 'Heterogeneous Multi-robot Task Allocation for Long-Endurance Missions in Dynamic Scenarios', T-RO 2025: coalition tasks, with plans repaired or recomputed online on unexpected events (MILP plus heuristic). https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.02062

Messing, Banfi, Stadler, Stump, Ravichandar, Roy, Hutchinson, 'A Sampling-Based Approach for Heterogeneous Coalition Scheduling with Temporal Uncertainty' (CS-HSSRG), RSS 2023, verified: sampled-scenario robust coalition schedules with a risk guarantee. https://www.roboticsproceedings.org/rss19/p107.html

D-ITAGS (Neville et al., RA-L 2023): targeted repair of coalition schedules after disruptions, at about the quality of re-solving. Gosrich et al., T-RO 2025 (arXiv 2509.15052): online coalition re-allocation beats the offline plan.

APEX-MR (Huang et al., RSS 2025, arXiv 2503.15836): a temporal plan graph gives asynchronous execution that is robust to delays without re-planning, including collaborative support actions. ADG (Hoenig et al., RA-L 2019) and SADG (Berndt et al.): key order and dependency graphs keep execution deadlock-free under delays. This is prior art for rule 2 and G1.

Vieira, Herrmann, Lin, 'Rescheduling Manufacturing Systems: A Framework of Strategies, Policies, and Methods', J. Scheduling 6(1) 2003: event-driven vs periodic rescheduling and schedule nervousness. The finding that noise does not justify re-planning and that cheap re-planning is nervous is textbook.

ACBBA timestamp and suffix-release rules, as restated in Lott and Honary, arXiv 2609.13711 (CV_MRTA degraded-comm benchmark), and the same authors' bundle-length study, arXiv 2609.06273: rule 5's consensus layer is ACBBA verbatim. CC-OPI (arXiv 2609.19208): versioned grow-only sets, action locks, event-driven re-auction under loss.

Mendoza, Su, Ferguson, Sastry, arXiv 2604.11954 (Apr 2026): dynamic MRTA with online arrivals, uncertain completion and communication constraints, decentralized best response vs SCoBA. Single-robot tasks only.

Unread HeteroMRTA citers that may pre-empt the dynamic HeteroMRTA gap: DODRL-HMRTA (Zeng et al., Neurocomputing 2026, doi 10.1016/j.neucom.2026.135060, 'learning-based optimization framework for HMRTA with dynamic uncertainties'); 'A Proactive Fault-Recovery Framework for Multi-Robot Task Allocation Using Successor Pre-Assignment' (CSCWD 2026); 'An LLM Based Framework for Automated MILP Modeling in Dynamic Multi-Robot Task Scheduling' (RA-L 2026). All were found through the Semantic Scholar citations API; no abstracts are accessible.

In-house prior pilots that already test KORE's C3 core: /home/jovyan/dev/cbba-sota/pilots/trackD_integ/out/summary.txt (P2-P8: LOC-F, CAS-INF and OPEN lose; CLAMP, HYB and a beacon win; lease sensitivity), /home/jovyan/dev/cbba-sota/pilots/trackD_comm2/out/dar34_summary.txt and vs_central_summary.txt (INF-r simple scope rule is best; DAR collapses), /home/jovyan/dev/cbba-sota/pilots/trackD/out/conn.txt (partners are usually within range).
redteam-1.minimal_change:
Stop presenting KORE as a new mechanism that beats the strongest baseline. Keep it only as a re-scoped, prespecified extension of the static result.

(1) Primary claim: event-sparse rolling-horizon coalition ALNS, i.e. the Phase-1 solver repairing only on structural events, is the online SOTA on externally anchored dynamic HeteroMRTA (R1 plus the LoRR delays, with F3 failures).
- Superiority tests: against the published RL online, RL re-rolled from the current state at every structural event (RL(s.N)-MPC), the RL64+ALNS hybrid online, RH-CP-SAT-LNS, and B6 (regret re-construction with restarts). All run at equal deterministic per-event iteration budgets and are replayed in DynTaskEnv.
- Central RH parity is stated as an identity, not tested by TOST.
- Report honestly that the RL margin is the static gap.

(2) Keep a C3 claim only if a 1-day kill pilot passes.
- Change first: replace rule 6 (frozen closure-local repair, which is the in-house LOC-F/CAS-INF that lost) with the variant that won: replicated ALNS on beliefs with a stale-state clamp (REP+CLAMP).
- Also: tune every method's lease on dev, add a low-rate global-beacon baseline and a suspicion-based failure detector.
- Pilot: D2 on MA-AT-25 and SA-BT-50, 10 dev instances x 2 seeds, with F3. Continue only if the ratio is <= 0.97 against min(CEN-F, REP, REP+beacon) with the CI excluding 1 in both settings. Otherwise report C3 as analysis only.

(3) Before any test run:
- anchor the failure horizon on the paper's RL makespan;
- make the 1 s tick co-primary;
- use a cluster bootstrap over instances;
- read DODRL-HMRTA and the CSCWD fault-recovery paper.

Probabilities of a clear margin:
- Design as written, over the strongest baseline: about 0.08.
- After the change, against the published RL and external-family online baselines: about 0.85, but this is mostly the inherited static gap.
- After the change, over the strongest in-house baseline via C3: about 0.15 to 0.2 (reported as p_clear_margin).

fatal: Collapse to simple rules in the fragmented primary cell. At R=0.1 (0.5-0.64 r_c), HALO cannot be told apart from three simpler arms: REP-v+clamp (B3), ungated HYB, and INF-r. INF-r is one rule: never give new work to unreachable robots and do not honour their stale future commitments. It was piloted earlier as P1 'Oh' / DAR 'INF-r' and then dropped from the B1-B8 list. I re-ran it on the exact P7/P8 dev grid (4 settings x 10 instances x 2 scenarios x 2 seeds; the CEN-F~G3:30 control reproduced the stored rows bit for bit, 640/640). Pooled n=160: INF-r/HALO is 0.972 [0.937, 1.007] with lease 3/30, 0.991 [0.960, 1.021] with 1/10 and 0.984 [0.955, 1.013] with 1/30. INF-r/CLAMP is 0.98-1.02. HALO/CEN-F is 0.839 [0.798, 0.881]. So the 16-18% gain over central comes from a generic rule: stranded components re-plan and ignore stale commitments of teammates they cannot reach. HALO's teammate model, station anchoring and gate add nothing measurable there. Files: /tmp/halo_rt/inf_lease.py, /tmp/halo_rt/inf_lease.jsonl, /tmp/halo_rt/inf_grid.jsonl, /tmp/halo_rt/analyze2.py.

The only HALO-specific component, the regime gate, is null. Paired against ungated HYB, HALO/HYB is 0.987, 0.991, 0.993, 1.032 for RN12 at R=0.3/0.2/0.15/0.1, and 0.918, 1.010, 0.996, 0.995 for RN3. Only one cell of eight is significant in HALO's favour, and it hurts by 3% at R=0.1 RN12. theta was picked post hoc from two values. Radio range and site size are known at deployment and connectivity is stationary within a HeteroMRTA episode (uniform task layout). A static per-deployment switch is therefore a realistic baseline, not an oracle, and it leaves the gate nothing to do. HALO's structure is the per-regime better of CEN-F and HYB, which is the CBJA failure mode (method equals the better of two baselines).

B1 is a strawman by construction. Its fallback set {idle, fixed greedy, rally} leaves out the obvious 'stranded component re-plans with the same ALNS' fallback. That fallback is exactly HYB, i.e. HALO without the gate. The task's own baseline definition ('central re-solve with local fallback') covers it. With it included, H3a's 10-15% effect would measure only the gate, which is about 0 +- 3%.

The primary cells avoid HALO's loss band. At exactly 1.0 r_c the pilot favours HALO: 0.953/0.934 on MA-AT-25 at R=0.2, and 0.986/0.929/0.960 (RN12) on the 50-robot settings at R=0.15. So H3b non-inferiority is nearly guaranteed. HALO trails CEN by 4-8% at about 1.27 r_c on 3 of 4 settings (R=0.2, 50 robots: SA-AT 1.082 [1.005, 1.172]; RN3 MA-AT-50 1.083 [1.006, 1.192], SA-AT 1.062, SA-BT 1.065). That band appears only in the diluted area-under-curve endpoint H3c. Reviewers will read the cell choice as selection after the pilot.

The makespan-only objective prices redundancy at zero, and the fragmented win is paid for in wasted travel. At R=0.1, HALO makes 42 wasted trips per 50-task episode, INF-r 51, CLAMP 43, CEN-F 3.4 (RN12). 'Redundancy beats consistency' is therefore a property of the objective. Any travel or energy endpoint, which a field reviewer will ask for, would probably shrink or reverse the fragmented advantage. CC-OPI (arXiv 2609.19208) already reports the same 'more messages and redundant travel for robustness' trade-off for island-fragmented swarms.
fixable: Makespan definition mismatch. The pilot scores hindsight_makespan: each robot is credited with leaving for its depot right after its last task, with no termination detection. The spec defines makespan as a physical return to the depot. Robots also know the total task count T (done_k[i].all() runs over every task id) under online release, which leaks knowledge. Fix: score the physical return with a termination rule under belief, and do not reveal T.

The lease is a ~10% lever even at ideal links: FULL(1/10)/FULL(3/30) = 1.084-1.106 on identical keys. Method rankings flip with it. INF-r vs CEN at R=0.3 was 0.988 against CEN with the 1/10 lease and 1.13 against CEN with 3/30. So K8 will probably fire. Fix the lease grid a priori, tune each method on dev, report the whole grid, and state claims as holding over the grid or not.

The true 0.5 r_c cell for the 50-robot settings (R about 0.078) was never piloted. The pilot's R=0.1 is 0.63 r_c there. In the only true 0.5 r_c pilot cell (MA-AT-25, RN12), HALO/CEN is 0.961 [0.852, 1.091], not significant.

The external channel models do almost nothing in T1. Loss is i.i.d. per link per tick at 10 Hz with instant flooding, so 20% loss adds about 0.025 time units of delay, and only range R matters. Make T2 (per-message loss, per-hop latency, byte budget) the only confirmatory tier. Show that the Bernoulli/GE/Rayleigh sweep moves results; otherwise stop presenting them as anchors.

The infrastructure beacon carries state only, which blocks central's plan downlink while helping replicated methods. Make the payload symmetric: every method may send any bytes up to the budget, and central may push routes. Under that rule central will probably dominate wherever a beacon exists, so say so.

The R-B release anchor is overstated. HeteroMRTA's 'reactive_planning' is a flag in the GIF animation code (third_party/HeteroMRTA/env/task_env.py ~L686-691) that only colours tasks. It is not env dynamics, so describe R-B as 'inspired by' the demo.

Hub-favouring world choices: a central station, releases only at the station, and a rally-to-station rule. Add a corner-station run, a multi-station run and spatially clustered task layouts as prespecified sensitivity cells.

All pilot effect sizes come from list scheduling + T1 + one lease. The full study changes planner (ALNS), channel (T2) and leases at once. Re-derive K1-K8 at D3 before freezing, and keep ALNS warm-started with commitments (the dar_pilot notes say cold-started in-loop ALNS churns and loses).
The 5% non-inferiority margin is larger than most measured effects (2-7%) and than the Phase-1 ALNS vs CP-SAT gaps (2-11%). Use 3% as primary, or justify 5% from deployment cost.

Missing published or obvious baselines: HYB-ungated; CEN + INF-r stranded rule; CEN-R + clamp; connectivity-aware CBBA with Relays (Ponda et al., JSAC 2012), which is the CBBA-lineage answer to range limits; rendezvous-rewarding planning (Bramblett et al., 2403.00641). Give each the same kernel and a dev-tuned lease.

K7 risk: RL on beliefs has no stale plan commitments. In the earlier trackD pilot its gap to open-loop ALNS shrank from 1.45 to 1.22 under severe noise. Run it in the comm world first. Also report RL with oracle state.

Compute accounting. HALO issues 1,200-1,500 planner calls per episode at R=0.1, against 105-128 for CEN. C2 holds per robot only, not per fleet. Wall-clock numbers taken on the overloaded shared host are invalid.
The CBBA lineage is only nominal (no auctions or winner tables). Position HALO as a replicated centralized solver (DGA/DMCHBA/implicit-coordination family) with a station anchor.
Multiplicity: H3a-e, H2a-d and the secondaries are each Holm-corrected only within their own hypothesis. Declare one confirmatory family.
prior_work: CC-OPI (arXiv 2609.19208, Sep 2026). Online, event-driven allocation for UAV swarms that short range fragments into 'information islands'; persistent partitioning; re-plans only at physical and topological events; explicitly trades more messages and redundant travel for robustness. Baselines are PI/CBBA variants and a Voronoi partition. Tasks are single-robot, not coalitions. It pre-empts HALO's qualitative C3 story.

CV_MRTA benchmark (arXiv 2609.13711, Sep 2026). Six decentralized allocators (CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA, DGA) under Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh impairments. DGA and DMCHBA, the replicated or knowledge-flooding styles, have the lowest mean MinMax under impairment. 'Replicated solver is strongest under degraded comm' is therefore already known for single-robot tasks.

Bramblett & Bezzo et al.: arXiv 2302.10393 (ICRA 2023), 2308.00579, 2403.00641 'Robust Online Epistemic Replanning of Multi-Robot Missions', and 2501.03907. Teammate-state belief propagation during comm loss; a centralized planner that rewards rendezvous, plus decentralized re-planning. This is the same diagnosis as HALO (teammate staleness), with planned rendezvous, which HALO lacks.

Ponda, Johnson, How et al., 'Distributed Planning Strategies to Ensure Network Connectivity for Dynamic Heterogeneous Teams' (IEEE JSAC 2012), CBBA with Relays. A connectivity-aware CBBA that uses under-used agents as relays; it is the CBBA-lineage baseline reviewers will expect.

DARPA SubT field architectures: ACHORD (Saboia et al., RSS 2022, arXiv 2206.02245), CSIRO Data61 (arXiv 2104.09053), CERBERUS (arXiv 2207.04914). Base-station planning while connected, autonomous operation and store-and-forward data mules when disconnected, return-to-comm behaviour. HALO's hub anchor, store-carry-forward and rally are standard field practice.
Otte, Kuhlman & Sofge, 'Auctions for multi-robot task allocation in communication limited environments', Autonomous Robots 2020. Auction families degrade differently as message loss grows.
Lott & Honary, arXiv 2609.06273. ACBBA/PI/HIPC bundle lengths tuned on ideal networks lose 7-14% under 25% loss, the same phenomenon as HALO's lease-sensitivity finding.
Calvo & Capitan, IEEE T-RO 2025 (arXiv 2411.02062). Heterogeneous coalitional MRTA with online plan repair or recomputation (centralized).
Mendoza et al., arXiv 2604.11954. Hub-based dynamic MRTA under communication constraints; iterative best response is competitive with centralized Hungarian allocation.

SADCHER (Bichler et al., MRS 2025, arXiv 2510.14851). Real-time dynamic heterogeneous coalition scheduling; a learned online alternative to the HeteroMRTA RL. Bezerra et al., arXiv 2412.20397: decentralized learned dynamic coalition formation from local information.

Replicated-state mechanism: CRDT literature (Shapiro et al.) and, as I recall but did not re-check this session, the Buzz 'virtual stigmergy' timestamped last-writer-wins tuple space for swarms (Pinciroli, Lee-Brown & Beltrame 2015). The max-merge replica is not novel.

No exact duplicate found: coalition (additive-trait) scheduling on HeteroMRTA under range-limited links with a replicated ALNS and a station anchor. Novelty is limited to the combination and the evidence, as the design itself says.
redteam-3.minimal_change:
Stop claiming a margin over the strongest baseline for C3, and give the claim an endpoint the pilot can actually support without cherry-picking.

(2) Make the primary C3 endpoint worst-case regret. For each method, take the maximum over R/r_c in {2, 1.5, 1.25, 1, 0.75, 0.5} of its paired log-ratio against the per-R best fixed architecture. - Clear SOTA margin (>= 5%, CI-separated) over the strongest equal-infrastructure baseline in a prespecified primary cell: about 0.10.
- The re-scoped minimax-regret claim separating from REP-clamp at test scale: about 0.3.

fatal: F1. The method is one of its own baselines. With theta=0 (the default, INF-r), SCOPE-RALNS lets the station plan its own component and lets the lowest live id plan every other component. That is exactly central rolling re-solve with a local fallback, where the fallback is the same solver run inside the disconnected component. The CEN-F baseline runs the same code path with a weakened fallback: freeze the route, then rally (pilots/trackD/integ_headroom.py, methods block). Given the natural fallback, the K2 comparison is 1.000 by construction. The scope rule itself has prior art. HIPC (Johnson, Choi & How, AIAA GNC 2013) is described in CV_MRTA as: 'Each robot forms a planning neighborhood from itself and peers whose behavior can be estimated from received state.' Bramblett et al. (IROS 2024, arXiv 2403.00641) split the workload among connected robots. C-CBBA and TLC-CBBA use cluster leaders. Demiray, Tolga & Yucel (arXiv 2309.09321, CIE 2026) already do warm rolling ALNS with frozen periods for dynamic synchronized multi-skill routing. The design itself concedes there is no mechanism novelty.

F2. The only measured communication margin, INF-r beating CEN-F by 5-9% at condition P, is an artifact of the lease setting. I re-ran the design's own pilot code; the wrapper reproduces dar3 bit-for-bit on 640/640 runs. The setup was 4 settings x 20 dev instances x 2 CRN seeds, with the lease at (grace 1, max 10) or (grace 3, max 30). Files: /tmp/redteam_trackD/lease_check2.py, lease_check2.jsonl, analyze.py, bestbest.py. The patient lease improves FULL by 7% (0.929), CEN-F and REP+ both prefer it, and INF-r is the only arm that prefers the short lease. At P with each arm at its better lease (picked in-sample from these two levels): INF-r/CEN-F = 1.001 [0.969, 1.035] (median 1.021); DTH1/CEN-F = 0.988 [0.959, 1.015]; REP+/CEN-F = 0.970 [0.938, 1.004]; INF-r/REP+ = 1.033 [1.003, 1.059]. So K2 fails and K3 fires, which makes the method the replicated solver. With both arms on the patient lease, INF-r/CEN-F = 1.085 [1.035, 1.141]. At R = 0.3 and 0.2, CEN-F beats INF-r by 8-9%. Scope helps only at R = 0.1 (0.5-0.63 r_c): INF-r/CEN-F = 0.849, but there it ties REP+ at 0.999. INF-r also makes about 10x the wasted trips (29.5 vs 2.4 at R = 0.15). Caveat: this uses the surrogate list-scheduling planner, not ALNS, and only 2 lease levels. The design's ETA lease has not been tested for any arm.

F3. Reviewers will read the benchmark as built for the method. At P the station reaches only 29-35% of the robots (pilots/trackD/out/conn.txt). Range was chosen as the stressor after the pilots showed loss does not matter. The design's own pilot (trackD_integ P5, REP-B1:0.2) shows that one global beacon per robot per 100 s, at 20% loss, cuts REP's loss at R = 0.15 from 1.238 to 1.078 of FULL. That beats INF-r (1.119, from a different pilot wave). One question, 'why no low-rate long-range telemetry such as LoRa?', therefore removes the only regime where scoping matters. The 'external anchors' only supply parameter values. The LoRR example delay is about a 2.5% slowdown, and CV_MRTA-style loss is shown to change nothing. The RGG radius r_c assumes uniformly placed nodes, but robots cluster at depots and at coalition sites. The 'R1 authors' batch-release demo' is a branch in the GIF renderer (task_env.py:686, reactive_planning=False by default) that only recolours tasks; it is not a benchmark feature. No third party has ever reported a number on HeteroMRTA-DC. This is the same self-defined-world pattern as the CBJA retro.

F4. The decision rule is underpowered and depends on tail events. E2 (TOST +-3% per setting, Holm): the per-instance SD of log(INF-r/REP+) near P is 0.07-0.31, so the 90% CI half-width at 50 instances is 1.6-7.7%. TOST power is 0-0.3 on 3 of 4 settings (0.63-0.75 only on SA-BT). The pilot's INF-r/REP+ = 0.929 at R = 0.15 has a median of 1.008. It is driven by 3/160 REP+ failures scored as 200. With failures excluded it is 0.956 (1.023 at R = 0.2). INF-r/CEN-F medians are 0.977-0.987 against means of 0.92-0.95.

F5. The design's own time mapping contradicts its real-time premise. At 1 time unit = 100 s, a 1-10 s central solve costs 1-10% of one time unit, so a slow central solver can run in real time. The 300-iteration (about 20 ms) per-event budget is arbitrary. A heavy central planner (ALNS or CP-SAT on 8 cores for seconds) is legal, so C2 does not separate anything in Track D.
fixable: Rolling ALNS does not exist yet. The cold in-loop version is 52% worse than open-loop. The warm version scores RH-A/OL-A 1.072 [1.032, 1.115] on MA-AT-25 under noise alone, so re-planning currently hurts. Make it a gate before any communication work: warm RH-ALNS must be at least as good as open-loop ALNS, and at least 5% better than RH-constructor, on the release-only dynamic dev set.

E3 (degradation D) is confounded by baseline quality and will likely go against ALNS. At sigma 0.3, ALNS-ol degrades 1.108-1.159 while RL degrades 1.017-1.028, and the RL/ALNS margin shrinks from 1.32-1.45 static to 1.18-1.29 (pilots/trackD/out/compact_table.txt). Replace it with absolute makespan at each connectivity level.

Treat the lease as a tuned factor for every arm, with an equal dev budget. Alternatively, validate one shared ETA lease on all arms. Extend K6 to cover ranking shifts caused by the lease, not only by the planner.

The RL-dec strawman: the static checkpoint is out of distribution under online arrivals and partial observation. Retrain RL in the DC env using the released Apache training code (4 H100s are available), or at least report RL-CEN under the best protocol.

CBTA-PR reimplementation in 1-2 days is unrealistic, and a rushed version will be a weak baseline. Budget at least a week, including a fidelity check on the setting of the CBTA paper (it should beat CBGA on average start time).

Statistics: use a cluster bootstrap by instance (3 CRN seeds per instance). Analyse success separately and do not impute 200 inside the ratio (keep that only as a sensitivity check). Report the median or Hodges-Lehmann estimate alongside the geometric mean. Size margins with power computed from the pilot SDs.
The pilot's hindsight makespan ignores termination-detection latency, which differs from HeteroMRTA's all-robots-home definition. Either use the physical definition or declare the change.
Report travel distance and wasted trips as co-primary metrics. INF-r is about 10x CEN-F on wasted trips.

Scope matters only when components are small, and small components are exactly where the ALNS-over-constructor gap should shrink, so the two margins do not add up. Measure RH-ALNS vs RH-constructor under partitions, not only with global information.
Before claiming the first dynamic HeteroMRTA study, read DODRL-HMRTA (Zeng et al., Neurocomputing 2026, doi 10.1016/j.neucom.2026.135060, 'dynamic uncertainties'). Its abstract could not be accessed.

Choose condition P as a prespecified average over R/r_c in {2, 1.25, 1, 0.75}, reporting the fraction of robots in the station's component, instead of a single point at the crossover. Include REP+ with a low-rate beacon, and a long-range downlink arm. Alternatively, restrict the claims to domains without long-range links (subterranean or underwater).
Measure CPU per event on quiet, pinned cores, with per-event budgets stated in physical seconds.
prior_work: HIPC, Hybrid Information and Plan Consensus (Johnson, Choi & How, AIAA GNC 2013, doi 10.2514/6.2013-4888): implicit planning for the local team, meaning the peers whose state was received, followed by plan consensus. This is the INF-r scope rule with a greedy planner.

Bramblett, Miloradovic, Sherman, Papadopoulos & Bezzo, Robust Online Epistemic Replanning of Multi-Robot Missions (IROS 2024, arXiv 2403.00641): workload is partitioned among connected robots, and robots keep beliefs about disconnected teammates (the DAR/DTH idea).

Demiray, Tolga & Yucel (arXiv 2309.09321; Computers & Industrial Engineering 2026): real-time rolling-horizon ALNS with frozen periods for dynamic multi-skill workforce routing with synchronization. This is warm rolling coalition ALNS with commitment.

CV_MRTA benchmark (Lott & Honary, arXiv 2609.13711): replicated-plan methods (DMCHBA, DGA) and HIPC lead under Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh loss. Tasks are single-robot, and no centralized reference is given.
Lott & Honary, bundle length under degraded communication (arXiv 2609.06273): HIPC stays in the deep-bundle regime under 25% loss.
CC-OPI (arXiv 2609.19208): versioned grow-only sets plus action locks for online allocation; nearly insensitive to loss. Tasks are single-UAV.
Clustered CBBA variants (C-CBBA, TLC-CBBA) and event-triggered adaptive consensus (Aznar et al., Computer Communications 2026, arXiv 2604.06813), whose baselines include C-CBBA and periodic CBBA.

CBTA (RA-L 2022), CBBA-PR (Buckman, Choi & How 2019), coupled-constraint CBBA (Whitten et al. 2011), D-ITAGS (RA-L 2023), and online coalition re-allocation (Gosrich et al., T-RO 2025, arXiv 2509.15052).
Recurrent or periodic connectivity (Hollinger & Singh; Banfi et al., Autonomous Robots 2018): prior art for the rally-to-station rule.
DODRL-HMRTA (Neurocomputing 2026), a HeteroMRTA citer with 'dynamic uncertainties'. Unread, and a potential dynamic-HeteroMRTA precedent.
Iterative Best Response for dynamic MRTA under communication constraints (Mendoza, Su, Ferguson & Sastry, arXiv 2604.11954).
redteam-2.minimal_change:
Drop SCOPE-RALNS as an algorithm contribution. Run Track D as a prespecified evaluation of the planner under a fixed protocol, with a best-vs-best primary endpoint.
(1) Name "central re-solve with component-local fallback" (= INF-r) as a shared, cited protocol (HIPC, Bramblett et al.), not as a contribution. Treat CEN-freeze, REP+, REP+ with a low-rate beacon, and DTH-theta only as descriptive protocol ablations.
(2) Primary claim is the planner main effect. Compare warm rolling ALNS against RH-constructor, rolling CP-SAT-LNS, CBTA-PR, released RL, and RL retrained in the DC env. Each gets its best protocol and its best lease, chosen on dev with an equal tuning budget. Give every arm the same per-event budget in physical seconds, and add an 8-core multi-second central solver as a reference.
(3) Gate first, on dev without any communication limits: warm RH-ALNS must be at least as good as open-loop ALNS and at least 5% better than RH-constructor under releases.
(4) Primary condition is the average over prespecified R/r_c values {2, 1.25, 1, 0.75}. Report the station-component fraction.
(5) Use a cluster bootstrap by instance, test success separately, and report median or Hodges-Lehmann estimates. Replace the per-setting +-3% TOST with a powered pooled margin.
(6) Report travel distance and wasted trips.
(7) Read DODRL-HMRTA before claiming novelty.

Probability estimates:
- A clear SOTA margin for the design as specified (mechanism or protocol claim): about 0.05.
- Its own decision rule (E1 plus E2 plus E4) passing on test: about 0.15.
- The re-scoped planner margin (at least 5%, CI below 1, on at least 3 of 4 settings, against the best non-ALNS planner at its best protocol and budget): about 0.3. This is limited by the unbuilt rolling ALNS, and by the gap to the constructor shrinking when components are small.
- Against the published RL alone: about 0.8, but reviewers will discount it.
